transcript.answer: Otto doesn't use the `global` endpoint because it would give up the EU data residency that Otto's model allowlist exists to enforce. The `global` endpoint does serve the Gemini 3.x family, but it doesn't guarantee requests are processed in the EU. The 3.x models aren't served from any single EU region. Their only options are `global` and, since 21 May 2026, the `eu` multi-region. Google's data-residency page documents the `eu` multi-region as the residency option for 3.x. The spec settled on 2026-10-16 to reject `global` and use `gemini-3.1-flash-lite` on the `eu` multi-region instead. That meant reaching the dedicated host `aiplatform.eu.rep.googleapis.com` through an `apiEndpoint` setting. The README says the provider block sets `apiEndpoint` from the region and startup refuses a block whose endpoint doesn't match its row's region. One caveat: the claim that `global` serves every Gemini model is only partly right. Models in the 2.5 family were served from `europe-west1`, which is how the earlier stopgap row stayed EU-resident.
